references.text: Jesus was in the habit of teaching in the synagogues. In [ref:Luk 4:15-16|Luke 4:15-16], it is described how he taught in the synagogues and entered the synagogue in Nazareth on the Sabbath day, as was his custom. This parallels his teaching in the synagogue on the Sabbath in Luke 13:10.
In [ref:Luk 4:31|Luke 4:31], Jesus went down to Capernaum and taught the people on the Sabbath days, showing his repeated practice of teaching in the synagogues on the Sabbath.
In [ref:Mark 1:21|Mark 1:21], Jesus enters the synagogue on the Sabbath and teaches. This confirms the pattern that Jesus used the Sabbath to preach in the synagogues.

In [ref:Mark 6:2|Mark 6:2], Jesus began to teach in the synagogue when the Sabbath came. This shows that Sabbath teaching in the synagogue was a central part of Jesus' ministry, as also seen in Luke 13:10.
In [ref:Matt 4:23|Matthew 4:23], Jesus' activity is described as going throughout Galilee and teaching the people in the synagogues. This provides the broader context for Jesus' synagogue teaching.

In [ref:Apg 13:14|Acts 13:14], Paul and Barnabas enter the synagogue on the Sabbath day – a practice that follows Jesus' own pattern of using the synagogue service as a framework for preaching (cf. [ref:Luk 13:10|Luke 13:10]).

The reaction of the synagogue ruler in [ref:Luk 13:14|Luke 13:14] confirms the context of verse 10 – that the event took place on the Sabbath in a synagogue, and that Jesus' healing there caused controversy over the Sabbath command.

In [ref:Apg 17:2|Acts 17:2], it is described that Paul, as was his custom, entered the synagogue and for three Sabbaths spoke to them from the Scriptures. This pattern goes back to Jesus' own practice of teaching in the synagogues on the Sabbath.
